newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs approve forest protection plans.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs approve forest protection plans.

text.p: The European Parliament agreed on Friday plans to prolong until 2001 existing measures to protect European Union forests from pollution and fire.
Under the renewed regulations, COM(96)341, 40 million Ecus will be made available for efforts to combat atmospheric pollution, largely through large-scale monitoring of forest ecosystems.
A further 70 million Ecus will be allocated to fire prevention schemes.

Rapporteur Ken Collins gave his backing on Thursday to calls by the London-based Environmental Investigation Agency for governments to agree at this year's Earth Summit II on a legally binding global agreement to conserve and sustainably manage the worlds' forests and regulate the timber industry.
A global forest convention was the only way to prevent the destruction of the world's remaining natural forests, the EIA said in a statement.
The parliament is due to vote on January 30 on plans for an EU policy on forests which marries the need to conserve Europe's forests with the pressure to exploit them commercially.
